subject: Next steps: proposed trial pathway and success criteria for BrightBridge
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@brightbridge.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightbridge.com
Date: 2027-04-30T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's demo — next steps

Thanks for the demo this morning — good overview and thanks to Ben for the deep-dive on latency and batching. A couple quick notes from our side and a request: 

- BrightBridge is interested in running a tight evaluation (4 week trial) focused on customer-service summarization workloads.
- Key internal stakeholders: Sophie (engineering lead), myself (product), procurement for terms.

Request: can you send a short proposed trial pathway that includes success criteria, a minimal data sample we'll need to provide, timeline, and clear owners on both sides? Procurement also asked for any network/security checklist up-front so they can start their review.

Appreciate a one-page outline we can circulate internally.

Tom
Tom Reyes
Director, Product — BrightBridge Financial
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@brightbridge.com>, Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightbridge.com
Date: 2027-04-30T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — next steps

Thanks Tom — appreciated the clear ask. Attached is a concise proposed trial pathway (redwood-poc-outline.pdf) but I summarized the key points below so you can circulate quickly.

POC Goal: Validate integration of Redwood Inference into BrightBridge's CS summarization pipeline with production-like latency and cost targets.

Scope (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (kickoff + onboarding): credentialing, test dataset handoff, brief infra checklist.
- Week 1: pilot run on 5k transcripts, validate latency and token-cost profile.
- Week 2: iterative prompt/temperature tuning, small-scale A/B with 10k requests/day.
- Week 3: run success evaluation, measure accuracy vs. baseline and cost per 1k tokens.
- Week 4: final review, handoff notes, optional extended trial next steps.

Success criteria (pass/fail style):
- Latency: P95 < 450ms for 1k-token requests under your typical concurrency.
- Quality: Rouge-L improvement >= 8% vs current rule-based summaries on the validation set.
- Cost: projected per-message cost reduction <= 30% vs your current third-party endpoint (based on our sample load).
- Reliability: 99% of requests return within SLA window across 3 test windows.

Owners and responsibilities:
- Redwood: Olga (trial lead, onboarding + evaluation), Ben (technical integration, infra notes), Evelyn (success metrics and enablement).
- BrightBridge: Tom (product owner), Sophie (engineering contact for dataset and deployment tests), procurement (contracts/terms).

Data & access
- Minimal sample: 5k de-identified transcripts in JSONL (fields: id, text, context). Ben will share a small example schema.
- Networking: we support VPC peering and temporary API keys; procurement requested our security sheet (attached: network-security-sheet.pdf).

Deliverables
- Week 0: onboarding checklist + test harness (Redwood).
- Week 2: interim metric snapshot + tuning notes (Redwood + BrightBridge).
- Week 4: final scorecard + handoff report (Redwood).

Proposed kickoff: Wednesday, 2027-05-05 @ 10:00 AM PT (30 minutes). If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include the onboarding checklist link.

Quick asks for you now:
1) Confirm stakeholders above and the kickoff slot.
2) Procurement: let us know any specific questions after a quick look at the attached security sheet.
3) Sophie: can you confirm whether the sample transcripts can be de-identified and shared to our secure intake bucket?

Thanks — happy to tighten any part of the plan.

— Olga Petrov

On Sat, May 1, 2027 at 08:45 AM Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@brightbridge.com> wrote:
> Thanks Olga — the plan looks reasonable and the success criteria are clear. A couple quick items from engineering/procurement: 
> 
> - We can share de-identified transcripts (will confirm by EOD).
> - Procurement asked: what is your default data retention for logs and KV cache? Is there an option to shorten retention during the trial?
> - Can you clarify whether the pilot will run against our infra via VPC peering or against Redwood-hosted endpoints? We prefer VPC peering if possible.

Thanks — quick answers below so procurement and Sophie have what they need: 

1) Data retention: default request/trace logs retained 30 days. We can configure reduced retention (7 days) for trials and/or provide a policy that auto-prunes request traces after the trial window. KV cache persistence is optional; by default it's in-memory across the session and not persisted long-term unless you opt-in.

2) Deployment mode: VPC peering is supported and preferred for customers that want network isolation — we can set that up for the trial. If VPC peering is not feasible immediately, we can run against Redwood-hosted endpoints with IP allowlist and TLS.

Next actions I'll take this week:
- Prepare a small example dataset schema and an S3 intake bucket instruction doc.
- Attach the network/security PDF used by our compliance team (network-security-sheet.pdf).
- Draft a 30-min kickoff agenda for Wednesday, 2027-05-05 @ 10:00 AM PT and send calendar invite pending confirmation.

Evelyn & Olga — if that timeline works, I’ll start prepping the test harness and a Slack channel for daily syncs during the trial.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
